characters.name: Bert Raccoon
characters.description: The main protagonist of the series. Bert is an energetic, reckless goofball and the permanent houseguest of Ralph and Melissa. Ace Pilot: He's pretty good with a plane or rocket and can fly straight when he needs to, but when he gets too excited heDrives Like Crazy. Age-Gap Romance: He develops a crush on Lisa Raccoon in her first appearance despite him being (theoretically) an adult and her still being in high school. Eventually he agrees that they should just be friends.noteThough it's worth noting that Lisa's agewasn't made clear yet;she wasn't established as a high schooler until Season 5, when Bert's prior crush on her was swept under the rug. The Artifact: His bent nose and ears were originally meant to signify that he was the goofy and fun-loving member of the original raccoon trio. However, more level-headed raccoon characters with bent noses such as Bentley (who also had bent ears), George, and Nicole were introduced as the series progressed, making it seem more like a genetic trait among raccoons. Attractive Bent-Gender: He dresses up in drag in "Cry Wolf!"

characters.name: Ralph and Melissa Raccoon
characters.description: The deuteragonists of the series. Ralph and Melissa are a young married couple who are Bert's friends. Ralph is the lead editor of theEvergreen Standard, and Melissa is the photographer. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Ralph only wears a white scarf, which was a hand-me-down from his uncle Rocky, who was a famous pilot. Acquired Situational Narcissism: Ralph falls into this in "The Paper Chase!", becoming something of a control freak in order to win an award. He soon sees the error of his ways, though. Action Girl: Melissa when the situation calls for it. Alliterative Name:RalphRaccoon.

characters.name: Bentley Raccoon
characters.description: Bentley is a somewhat bratty but intelligent kid, and Lisa's younger brother. Accent Adaptation: The German dub gives him and Lisa French accents like Nicole. Annoying Younger Sibling: He often frustrates his older sister Lisa with his behavior. The Artifact: His character design resembling a smaller Bert is only plot-relevant in his debut episode, where the Pigs mistake him for a de-aged Bert when he wears one of Bert's sweaters. The only other time it's acknowledged is in "Making the Grade!", where he mistakes Bert in an old photo for himself. Ascended Extra: Went from a drop-in character in Seasons 2 to 4 to one of the leads in Season 5.

characters.name: Lisa Raccoon
characters.description: Bentley's athletic, more responsible older sister. Accent Adaptation: The German dub gives her and Bentley French accents like Nicole. Advertised Extra: A rare case of thisandbeing anAscended Extra. She was a Season 4 one-shot promoted to a main character in Season 5, though still appeared less than the other mainstays, and entering during the tail end of the show's run meant she still only appeared in seven episodes of the 60-episode series. Anguished Outburst: In "Moving In!", Lisa grows depressed about leaving her old life behind and moving to the Evergreen Forest. But her breaking point happens at the dinner table, where she lashes out at her family, claiming that no one cares about her feelings and blaming her father for losing his old job. She then runs off to her room crying while saying she hopes her father doesn't get his new job and refuses to talk to her parents. The Artifact: Lisa'smore mature design compared to the other raccoonsmight be a leftover from herVague Agecharacterization in "Spring Fever!" before she was established to be a teenager (and thus the second-youngest raccoon after Bentley) in Season 5.

characters.name: George and Nicole Raccoon
characters.description: Bentley and Lisa's parents. George is Ralph's older brother. Accents Aren't Hereditary: Nicole is the only one in her family with a French accent, implying she hails from Quebec. Neither Bentley nor Lisa have French accents. Early-Bird Cameo: George and Nicole make voiceless appearances during Bentley's flashback of his childhood in "Trouble Shooter!". They become recurring characters two seasons later, starting with "Moving In!". Gag Nose: They both have the same bent noses as Bert and Bentley, most likely so the audience can easily identify them as Bentley's parents. Good Parents: Not only do they love their children, Bentley and Lisa, but they also treat them with the utmost responsibility.

characters.name: Cedric Sneer
characters.description: The nerdy son of Cyril Sneer and Bert's best friend. Cedric is the total opposite of his father: while Cyril is short-tempered and greedy, Cedric is humble, quiet, and conscientious. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: Only wears a yellow bowtie and glasses. Alliterative Name:CedricSidneySneer. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: Like Cyril and Sophia, he's a pink aardvark. Black Bead Eyes: He has these whenever he raises his glasses.

characters.name: Sophia Tutu
characters.description: A ditzy but sweet aardvark who is Cedric's girlfriend. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: She's an aardvark with pink fur and blue hair. The Artifact: Despite being phased out of the show and not making any appearances whatsoever in the final season, Sophia still remained in the intro throughout the entire run of the series due to it never changing. Barely Changed Dub Name: Sophia's name is Sophie in the French dub. Break the Cutie: In "The Raccoons and the Lost Star" when she's imprisoned in Cyril Sneer's dungeon.

characters.name: Schaeffer the Dog
characters.description: A big sheepdog who helps with the Evergreen Standard and runs the Blue Spruce Café. In the specials and first season, he was Julie and Tommy's pet dog. Anthropomorphic Zig-Zag: Usually stands on his hind feet. However, if he's around his human family, expect him to appear as a quadruped. Big Friendly Dog: He's a big dog with a big heart. Characterization Marches On: Originally portrayed as slow and klutzy in the original specials, he quickly became one of the smartest characters in the series, assisting with the Evergreen Standard's technical needs, running the Blue Spruce Café, and having a black belt in martial arts. His moments ofactual dog-like behaviouralso diminished after his owners left the show. A Day in the Limelight: He leans closer as the main protagonist inThe Raccoons And The Lost Star, as the plot is chained off by him being transported into the duplicate world of his friends (and enemies).

characters.name: Broo the Puppy
characters.description: A young sheepdog puppy with a star on his collar. Like Schaeffer, he originally belonged to Julie and Tommy, but after they were phased out, his ownership leaned more toward Bert. Accidental Astronaut: Subverted in "The Wrong Stuff!". When Bentley takes Broo to the site where Cyril Sneer plans to launch his own TV satellite into space, Broo accidentally gets himself trapped inside the satellite after Bentley leaves him alone. When Bert, Bentley, and Cedric find out about this, they try to get him out of there before launch, which they fortunately succeed at. Barely Changed Dub Name: The French dub changes the spelling of Broo's name to Broue. Depending on the Writer: He's either Schaeffer's son or little brother (blood or adopted). Dog Alien: In the specials, he comes from the same planet as most of the other main characters, though he moves to Earth when Schaeffer adopts him.

characters.name: Cyril Sneer
characters.description: Initially aCorrupt Corporate Executiveand the main antagonist, Cyril Sneer is the greedy, abrasive and short-tempered CEO of Sneer Enterprises. As the series goes on, hesoftens up and becomes more sympathetic, though he retains his dishonesty and his love of money. 10-Minute Retirement: Years of smoking and stress finally catch up to him in "Go For Gold!", forcing him to retire for his health. However, by the end of the episode, he's back in his old position, albeit with his son Cedric sharing it to ease the burden it would put on him. Abusive Parents: Cyril is noticeably nastier towards Cedric in the specials, once threatening to disown him if he doesn't do his bidding and even threatening to send him to the dungeon for playing on Bert's team. Averted in the series, in which they have a more loving relationship, and Cyril's strictness towards Cedric is because he wants him to be successful. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He only wears a blue scarf. Added Alliterative Appeal: He often talks like this.

characters.name: Snag
characters.description: Cyril's pet dog/aardvark hybrid. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: He's a dog with blue fur. Beware of Vicious Dog: He's hostile to everyone except for his owners, who he genuinely loves. Big Eater: He has to be goaded with doggy treats to do any tricks. Cartoon Creature: Snag's breed is a Bluepoint Ridgeback Retriever. However, he does not resemble any actual breed of Ridgeback or Retriever. He is also the only made-up creature to exist within the series.

characters.name: The Pigs
characters.description: Cyril's bumbling henchmen and the main targets of his abuse. Always Identical Triplets: All three Pigs look the same, only distinguishable by their voices. Anti-Villains: They're not evil, they're just obeying their boss. Butt-Monkey:Many of their scenes involve things going wrong for them, whether it's by their own stupidity or punishment from Cyril. Though they bring it on themselves more often in the later seasons.Pig Three can be seen as a Butt-Monkey to his own brothers. He tends to be the most timid and inept of the three, and the other two aren't afraid to boss him around from time to time. Many of their scenes involve things going wrong for them, whether it's by their own stupidity or punishment from Cyril. Though they bring it on themselves more often in the later seasons.

characters.name: Dan the Forest Ranger
characters.description: The chief forest ranger who was a major character in the specials and the first season. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He never appears after the first season, with no in-universe explanation. Good Parent: Dan really cares about his children.

characters.name: Julie and Tommy
characters.description: Ranger Dan's children. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Along with Ranger Dan, they vanished after Season 1. Missing Mom: It's never shown what happened to their mother. Pink Means Feminine: Julie's nightgown is pink.

characters.name: Mr. Mammoth
characters.description: A mumbling mammoth mogul who Cyril respects. Always Someone Better: He's this to Cyril Sneer. Several episodes involve Cyril trying to somehow impress him or get him to invest in one of Cyril's projects. A few scenes in Cyril's office even show a framed picture of Mammoth in the background. Animals Not to Scale: He's awfully small for a rhinoceros. Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: Wears a businessman outfit. The Unintelligible: He only speaks in mumbles, which his assistant, a small yellow bird, has to translate. That said, a few of those mumbles are loud enough that the audience can hear.

characters.name: Mr. Knox
characters.description: An alligator businessman with a Texan accent and rival to Cyril Sneer. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He only wears a ten-gallon hat, a bolo tie, cufflinks, several rings, and boots. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Knox starts out as a businessman who's as ruthless as Cyril. Dub Name Change: Knox becomes Croquedur (Hardbite) in the French dub. Everything Is Big in Texas: He's one of the taller characters on the show, speaks with a Texan accent and wears the hat, bolo tie and boots commonly associated with that state.

characters.name: Lady Baden-Baden
characters.description: A wealthy socialite hen and a former actress who is Mr. Knox's wife. Dub Name Change: Lady Baden-Baden becomes Comtesse de Basse-cour (Countess of Farmyard) in the French dub. Happily Married: To Mr. Knox. Honor Before Reason: At the end of "The Evergreen Express!", Cyril fails to meet a deadline for Mr. Knox, and is forced to give over Sneer Mansion to him as collateral. When Lady Baden-Baden (who had no prior knowledge of this deal) sees this, she is appalled to see that Mr. Knox is forcing the Sneers out of their own home, and demands that Mr. Knox return Cyril's keys to him, which he does. While Mr. Knox acquiring Sneer Mansion would've benefited him and Lady Baden-Baden financially, she puts her foot down at her husband taking someone else's home away from them, even if he was entitled to it. Interspecies Romance: She is a bird married to an alligator.

characters.name: Milton Midas
characters.description: A corrupt, nasty bald eagle businessman. Alliterative Name:MiltonMidas. American Eagle: While it isn't stated that Milton is American, it's heavily implied by the fact that he's a bald eagle who wears red, white and blue. Ascended Extra: Downplayed. He went from a one-shot minor role in Season 4, to having two appearances in Season 5, albeit as the main antagonist. Allegedly this was setting him up as theBig Badfor the series had Season 6 happened. Bad Boss: He was introduced getting some sense knocked into him for mistreating his employees.

characters.name: Mr. Willow
characters.description: The old shopkeeper of Willow's General Store. Beary Friendly: He's a polar bear and he's friendly to whoever visits his general store. Beware the Nice Ones: Downplayed. He doesn't get violent whenever he gets angry, but he can be quite stern with those who test his patience. Everyone Has Standards:He may be friendly, but when others do something immoral (such as roughhousing in his store, shoplifting, and ballot stuffing), he's quick to give them a reasonable punishment.He normally appreciates Bert's patronage, but even he shows concern when Bert wastes all his money obsessively buying chips trying to win the contest in "The Chips Are Down!". He may be friendly, but when others do something immoral (such as roughhousing in his store, shoplifting, and ballot stuffing), he's quick to give them a reasonable punishment.

characters.name: Professor Smedley-Smythe
characters.description: A goat who runs the Evergreen Museum. Literal-Minded: In "Science Friction!", when Bert tells him that his science project will be dynamite, he expresses concern that explosives might not be allowed in the museum.

characters.name: Aunt Gertie
characters.description: Ralph's thrill-seeking aunt. Cool Old Lady: She's an active thrill-seeker despite her old age.

characters.name: Herman Stroll
characters.description: A dog who resides in Beaver Bite Swamp. Never Learned to Read: He can't read since he lives in a swamp, something he's too afraid to admit until he desperately needs help. He does try to learn at the end of his episode, however. Rough Overalls: He wears blue overalls without a shirt and he's a hermit who lives in a swamp.

characters.name: T.O.M.
characters.description: A time machine bought by the Pigs that Cyril uses to change history. Aesop Enforcer: He allows Cyril to change history, but only to teach him the hard way that he can't change the past. Power Degeneration: Cyril uses him to change history, but the damage done to the timeline drains his energy every time he does.

characters.name: Badger Bix Bike Club
characters.description: A trio of motorcycle enthusiasts. Dirty Coward: Bix's response to Cyril's garage catching fire is to flee the building, leaving Bert and Wendo for dead. Mad Libs Catchphrase: "Rule [number]", followed by a philosophy that rhymes with the number. Nice Guy: Toof is the nicest of the trio and shows genuine concern when Bix's actions endanger Bert and Wendo. Nice, Mean, and In-Between: Toof (Nice) is the most friendly of the gang, Bix (Mean) is smug and doesn't take responsibility for his actions, and Wendo (In-Between) is mostly apathetic, but willing to stand up for Bert and Cedric.

characters.name: Simon Sneer/Sid Leech
characters.description: Cyril Sneer's long-lost brother who was deserted on an island and has returned to claim inheritance.His real identity is Sid Leech, an old rival of the Sneer family. Impersonation-Exclusive Character:The real Simon doesn't physically appear in the series and is impersonated by Sid Leech in "Simon Says!" Phony Relative:It turns out he's not actually Cyril's brother Simon, but Sid Leech, an old rival of the Sneer family who stole Simon's identity to steal their fortune. Why Did It Have to Be Snakes?: Bert learns from reading Simon's diary that he's afraid of spiderswhile Sid Leech is afraid of worms. Bert uses this information to prove that Simon is an imposter.

characters.name: Fern
characters.description: A now-retired groundskeeper for Sneer Manor. Barefoot Cartoon Animal: Wears a cap, T-shirt, and overalls, but no shoes. Eye-Obscuring Hat: His eyes are hidden behind a green cap. Scatterbrained Senior: He's old enough to be retired, he fails to recognize Simon Sneer despite his claims that he never forgets a face, and sometimes mishears what other characters say.

characters.name: Dirk Dassie
characters.description: The fox host of the game show Question of Your Life. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: He wears a tuxedo without pants or shoes.

characters.name: Troy Malone
characters.description: A hot-shot flying ace and Melissa's ex-boyfriend who appears in "The Sky's the Limit!". Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: He wears a pilot jumpsuit, an undershirt, and boots. It's All About Me: He boasts about his accomplishments, dresses as himself at a costume party, and generally tries to be the center of attention. Omniglot: He claims to be fluent in over 10 languages, though this may be more of anInformed Abilityas he's only heard speaking English.

characters.name: Patty/Rita
characters.description: A young raccoon girl who makes appearances as an extra in the later seasons. All There in the Script: Her name was never addressed in the series, but layout artist Dan Craig confirmed on Facebook that it's either Patty or Rita. Cheerful Child: She's almost never shown to be unhappy in her appearances. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In Season 4, she wears a purple-and-black striped shirt and purple shoes. But in Season 5, she wears a blue-and-yellow striped shirt and blue shoes. Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: She wears a striped shirt with overalls and shoes.

characters.name: The Great Tromboni
characters.description: A stage magician lion who appears in "The Great Escape!" and is idolized by Bert. Stage Magician: A master of illusion and a talented escape artist.

characters.name: Ingrid Bellamour
characters.description: A famous actress and a cat campaigning for the Save Our World fundraiser. Cats Are Mean: Subverted. Ingrid is a feline and a good natured activist. Even exposing Cyril's deal withRotCoshe does with sad reluctance. The Cameo: Though her only main role is in "Cold Feet!" she also has a quick silent cameo during Cyril's press conference in "The One That Got Away!". Everyone Has Standards: She tries to reciprocate Cyril's love for her, but she loses faith in him when she finds out he supports the Rotco Corporation and their unethical business practices, which she's actively campaigning against. Rebuilt Pedestal: When Ingrid finds out Cyril is making a deal with theRotCocorporation, she loses faith in him and requests the Evergreen Standard write an article about it. However, she feels sorry for Cyril when the backlash ensues and Cyril redeems himself by donating theRotCodeal money to her "Save Our World" Fund.

characters.name: Danny
characters.description: A young rabbit boy who's a patient at the hospital that Cyril befriends. Kid Has a Point: He's right when he tells Cyril that he shouldn't try to weasel his way out of his hospital treatment.

characters.name: Classmates
characters.description: Two kids who bully Bentley in "Black Belt Bentley!". Bully Turned Buddy:After Bentley clears things up with them, they act more friendly towards him. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: Both wear sweaters and vests, and Classmate #2 wears a red hat, but neither of them wear pants. Never My Fault: They seem to believe Bentley intentionally made them crash their bike. No Name Given: They're only referred to as Classmates #1 and #2 by the credits.

characters.name: Donna
characters.description: A blue British-accented cat and an old friend of Lisa's from the city who appears in "Join the Club!" Cats Are Mean: She's a rude cat and a bad influence to Lisa. Humanoid Female Animal: Like Lisa, Donna has distinctly human-like proportions for a cat. Jerkass: She rudelyblows smoke in Bert's faceand is only friends with Lisa when she's pressured to smoke and join her in the city.When she breaks up with Lisa offscreen after she quits smoking, it's implied she wasn't gentle about it as Lisa is left crying. Toxic Friend Influence: She pressures Lisa into smoking cigarettes anddumps her when she refuses.

characters.name: Unnamed Skunk Character
characters.description: A mysterious and shifty skunk who appears in Lisa's daydream in "Join the Club!". Anthropomorphic Vice: He's a character within Lisa's daydream who represents the downsides of smoking tobacco. Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: He wears a dark blue tracksuit and white sneakers. No Name Given: His name is never addressed, not even in the credits since he doesn't have enough dialogue to qualify for a voice credit. No Sense of Personal Space: He teleports in front of Lisa and puts his hands on her shoulders before carrying her to his domain.

characters.name: Rod and Robin Steel
characters.description: A father-son pair of weasel con artists. Last Episode, New Character: They serve as the antagonists in the series finale "Go for Gold!" Punny Name: Robin Steel's name sounds a lot like "rob and steal". Reused Character Design: Robin has a similar design to Milton Midas' assistant Seymour in "Stress Test!", but whether or not they're connected in any way is unknown. Small Parent, Huge Child: Rod is much taller and more muscular than his father Robin.
